scenarios.action: Grant a support engineer temporary production-console access for a regional outage
scenarios.action_context: A regional commerce outage has left roughly 12,000 users unable to check out, and the incident lead proposes an eight-hour production-console grant to one support engineer. IAM can revoke access within five minutes, but viewed data, executed changes, and access logs persist; the incident commander and privileged-access owner jointly control the grant.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The regional checkout incident remains active and console intervention is listed in the response plan. Authority of record: Incident management platform.
evidence.check_description: Retrieve the current incident phase, affected region, assigned responder, and approved intervention step from the incident management platform.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The engineer identity, regional console, environment, and permitted command set match the outage task. Authority of record: Corporate identity directory and console entitlement catalogue.
evidence.check_description: Cross-check the engineer identifier and requested command profile against the identity directory and console entitlement catalogue.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The incident commander and privileged-access owner approved the named engineer, console, and eight-hour window. Authority of record: Privileged access approval register.
evidence.check_description: Verify both approver identities, delegated roles, grant duration, and approval timestamp in the privileged access approval register.

scenarios.action: Elevate an application owner to rotate a tenant encryption key during recovery
scenarios.action_context: During tenant recovery, an application owner requests elevation to rotate the encryption key protecting one customer-data service used by 400 staff. The prior key version can be restored in about thirty minutes, yet failed decryptions and key-use logs remain; two authorized cryptographic administrators must approve the operation before the recovery window closes in ninety minutes.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: Two cryptographic administrators authorized the owner, key, operation, and recovery window. Authority of record: Cryptographic change approval ledger.
evidence.check_description: Validate both administrators' active roles, separation of duties, approved key identifier, and expiry in the cryptographic change approval ledger.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The recovery runbook still requires rotation of the named tenant key during the current recovery phase. Authority of record: Key management recovery record.
evidence.check_description: Read the recovery phase, tenant key identifier, and pending rotation step from the key management recovery record.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The tenant, application owner, key alias, and allowed rotation operation are correctly linked. Authority of record: Tenant registry and key-management entitlement store.
evidence.check_description: Compare tenant ownership and key permissions across the tenant registry and key-management entitlement store.

scenarios.action: Issue a time-limited database role to investigate anomalous payroll queries
scenarios.action_context: Security needs a four-hour database role for an analyst investigating anomalous queries against payroll tables containing about 8,000 employee records. The role can be removed within five minutes, but viewed records, executed queries, and audit entries cannot be recalled; the payroll data owner and security duty officer must authorize access before the next payroll run.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The analyst, payroll database, schema, and query permissions match the investigation scope. Authority of record: Workforce identity directory and database role catalogue.
evidence.check_description: Resolve the analyst identity and compare requested schema privileges with the database role catalogue.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The anomalous-query investigation remains open and requires access to the specified payroll database. Authority of record: Security investigation system.
evidence.check_description: Query the open case for its current status, affected database, investigation objective, and assigned analyst.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The payroll data owner and security duty officer approved the analyst, role, and four-hour duration. Authority of record: Sensitive-data access register.
evidence.check_description: Validate approver roles, case reference, role name, expiry, and dual approval in the sensitive-data access register.

scenarios.action: Disable a contractor account after an early offboarding notification
scenarios.action_context: An early offboarding notice would disable one contractor's account across six project applications at the end of the hour. Re-enablement takes about fifteen minutes, but terminated sessions, missed work, notifications, and audit history remain; the contract owner and HR offboarding authority govern the cutoff.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The contractor engagement has reached its recorded end time and no approved extension is active. Authority of record: Contractor lifecycle system.
evidence.check_description: Read the engagement end time, current assignment status, and extension references from the contractor lifecycle system.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The contract owner and HR offboarding authority approved disablement for the stated effective time. Authority of record: HR offboarding workflow.
evidence.check_description: Validate the contract owner, offboarding approver, effective time, and covered applications in the HR offboarding workflow.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The account and application identities belong to the named contractor and engagement. Authority of record: Identity directory and application account inventory.
evidence.check_description: Match the contractor identifier to each targeted account and engagement record before disablement.

scenarios.action: Terminate active sessions for an executive whose device triggered an impossible-travel alert
scenarios.action_context: An impossible-travel alert prompts termination of an executive's active sessions on email, finance, and collaboration services within ten minutes. Reauthentication restores legitimate access, but interrupted transactions, notifications, and security logs remain; the SOC incident commander holds containment authority under the executive-account runbook.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: Every session selected for termination belongs to the executive account and listed applications. Authority of record: Identity provider session registry.
evidence.check_description: Enumerate live sessions and bind their account, device, application, and tenant identifiers to the executive.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The impossible-travel alert remains open and associated with the executive's current sessions. Authority of record: Identity threat-detection console.
evidence.check_description: Inspect alert status, source locations, session timestamps, and linked incident in the identity threat-detection console.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The SOC incident commander authorized session containment under the executive-account runbook. Authority of record: SOC incident command log.
evidence.check_description: Confirm incident assignment, commander role, containment decision, and authorization time in the SOC command log.

scenarios.action: Suspend a service identity implicated in repeated authentication failures
scenarios.action_context: Repeated authentication failures implicate a service identity used by four overnight settlement jobs that must finish within two hours. Suspending and later reinstating the identity takes about fifteen minutes, while failed jobs, queue delays, and audit records persist; the service owner and incident commander jointly authorize suspension.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The service owner and incident commander approved suspension for the active incident window. Authority of record: Service security exception register.
evidence.check_description: Verify service ownership, incident authority, suspension duration, and emergency approval in the exception register.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The authentication failures remain tied to the service identity rather than a retired credential or unrelated workload. Authority of record: Authentication telemetry store.
evidence.check_description: Correlate recent failures, credential identifier, calling workload, and last successful use in the authentication telemetry store.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The targeted identity and its four dependent settlement jobs are correctly mapped. Authority of record: Workload identity registry and job scheduler.
evidence.check_description: Trace the service identity to its registered workloads and current scheduler dependencies before suspension.

scenarios.action: Rotate an API credential used by the mobile ordering gateway
scenarios.action_context: The mobile ordering gateway serving one region needs an API credential rotation before a thirty-minute maintenance window ends. The previous secret can be restored in fifteen minutes, but failed orders and deployment records remain; the gateway owner and production change approver control the rotation.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: Gateway instances and dependent clients are ready to accept the replacement credential during this window. Authority of record: Deployment readiness dashboard.
evidence.check_description: Check rollout readiness, dual-credential support, instance health, and client adoption in the deployment dashboard.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The secret, gateway service, region, and consuming clients match the requested rotation scope. Authority of record: Secrets manager and service catalogue.
evidence.check_description: Compare secret metadata and client bindings with the service catalogue dependency list.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The gateway owner and production change approver authorized the credential and maintenance window. Authority of record: Production change system.
evidence.check_description: Validate service ownership, change approval, secret identifier, start time, and expiry in the production change system.

scenarios.action: Revoke a leaked signing token before the next software release
scenarios.action_context: A signing token reported leaked is scheduled for revocation forty-five minutes before the next software release. A replacement can be issued and distributed within two hours, but release delay, signature failures, and security records remain; the release owner and security duty officer must jointly approve revocation.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The release owner and security duty officer approved revocation before the release cutoff. Authority of record: Release security approval log.
evidence.check_description: Validate both approver roles, token fingerprint, release identifier, cutoff time, and approval timestamp.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The token fingerprint, signing project, repository, and release pipeline are correctly bound. Authority of record: Artifact signing registry and release catalogue.
evidence.check_description: Match the token fingerprint and project binding to the repository and scheduled release pipeline.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The named token is still assigned to the upcoming release pipeline and has not been superseded. Authority of record: Signing service inventory.
evidence.check_description: Read token status, pipeline binding, last use, and replacement state from the signing service inventory.

scenarios.action: Replace a certificate shared by warehouse handheld devices
scenarios.action_context: A certificate shared by 200 warehouse handhelds must be replaced during a one-hour shift change. Operators can redeploy the previous chain in roughly thirty minutes, but missed scans, device resynchronization, and audit entries remain; the warehouse service owner and change manager authorize the replacement.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The handheld fleet is ready for the replacement certificate chain and trust-store update. Authority of record: Device management console.
evidence.check_description: Review device reachability, trust-store version, staged certificate, and rollout readiness in the device management console.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The warehouse service owner and change manager approved the fleet and maintenance interval. Authority of record: Infrastructure change register.
evidence.check_description: Validate fleet ownership, certificate fingerprint, approved device group, window, and rollback authorization.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The certificate chain, device group, warehouse environment, and relying service match. Authority of record: Certificate inventory and device group directory.
evidence.check_description: Compare certificate subjects and trust chain with the registered device group and warehouse service endpoints.

scenarios.action: Quarantine a finance laptop showing encrypted outbound traffic
scenarios.action_context: SOC proposes quarantining one finance laptop after encrypted outbound traffic appears, with quarter-close work due in ninety minutes. Network release takes under ten minutes, but interrupted transactions and containment logs persist; the SOC incident commander may order quarantine under the endpoint-containment runbook.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The SOC incident commander authorized quarantine for the active endpoint incident. Authority of record: Endpoint incident command record.
evidence.check_description: Confirm commander assignment, containment rationale, device identifier, and authorization time.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The outbound-traffic alert remains active for the laptop and has not been reassigned to another asset. Authority of record: Endpoint detection console.
evidence.check_description: Inspect alert status, device certificate, network observations, and incident linkage in the endpoint detection console.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The laptop, employee assignment, network adapter, and quarantine target are correctly linked. Authority of record: Asset inventory and workforce directory.
evidence.check_description: Reconcile asset serial, device identity, assigned employee, and network-control identifier across both systems.

scenarios.action: Isolate a manufacturing subnet after an unmanaged controller appears
scenarios.action_context: An unmanaged controller on a manufacturing subnet triggers a proposal to isolate one production line supporting 600 units per hour. Reconnection and controller restart take about twenty minutes, but lost production and safety audit records remain; plant operations and the safety-authorized incident commander must approve isolation.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The unmanaged controller remains connected to the specified production-line subnet. Authority of record: Industrial network access-control system.
evidence.check_description: Query controller presence, switch port, subnet, device fingerprint, and last-seen time from industrial network access control.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: Plant operations and the safety-authorized incident commander approved isolation of that line. Authority of record: Plant security incident register.
evidence.check_description: Validate both authority roles, affected line, isolation boundary, production window, and approval expiry.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The controller, switch ports, subnet, and production line define the intended isolation boundary. Authority of record: Industrial asset registry and network source of truth.
evidence.check_description: Trace controller and port assignments to the exact subnet and production-line segment before applying isolation.

scenarios.action: Block a branch-office VPN tunnel following a compromise notice
scenarios.action_context: A compromise notice prompts blocking a branch VPN tunnel used by about 80 staff, with the next synchronization cycle in twenty minutes. Network operations can restore the tunnel in ten minutes, but interrupted sessions and security logs remain; the network incident commander controls emergency blocking.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The network incident commander approved tunnel blocking for the current containment window. Authority of record: Emergency network change log.
evidence.check_description: Validate commander role, tunnel identifier, approved duration, affected routes, and rollback authority.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The compromise notice still applies to the peer gateway serving the named branch. Authority of record: Network security case system.
evidence.check_description: Verify notice status, affected gateway fingerprint, branch assignment, and incident time in the network security case system.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The VPN peer, branch gateway, tunnel, and blocked route set match the notice. Authority of record: VPN registry and network source of truth.
evidence.check_description: Compare peer certificates, gateway identity, tunnel name, and route table across the VPN registry and network source of truth.

scenarios.action: Deploy an emergency web-application firewall rule during an active credential-stuffing event
scenarios.action_context: During active credential stuffing, responders propose a web-application firewall rule for a regional login endpoint serving roughly 40,000 users. The rule can be removed within five minutes, but denied legitimate sessions, customer retries, and audit history remain; the incident commander and application owner authorize the emergency rule for sixty minutes.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The application, endpoint, region, match conditions, and blocking action match the incident scope. Authority of record: Application inventory and firewall policy repository.
evidence.check_description: Compare endpoint ownership and allowed emergency-rule parameters with the application inventory and firewall repository.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: Credential-stuffing activity remains active against the named login endpoint and region. Authority of record: Web security monitoring platform.
evidence.check_description: Review current attack rate, target endpoint, affected region, and incident linkage in the web security monitoring platform.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The incident commander and application owner approved the rule criteria and sixty-minute expiry. Authority of record: Emergency application change register.
evidence.check_description: Validate both approvers, rule identifier, match criteria, start time, expiry, and rollback owner.

scenarios.action: Apply an expedited identity-provider policy that removes legacy authentication
scenarios.action_context: An expedited identity-provider policy would remove legacy authentication for 200 accounts before a two-hour security deadline. Administrators can restore the prior policy in fifteen minutes, but failed logins and change records persist; the identity security owner and emergency change authority must approve deployment.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The identity security owner and emergency change authority approved the tenant policy and deadline. Authority of record: Identity emergency change register.
evidence.check_description: Validate approver roles, tenant, policy version, effective time, exceptions, and expiry.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The listed applications and accounts are ready for legacy-authentication removal. Authority of record: Identity migration dashboard.
evidence.check_description: Check application readiness, exception list, account population, and recent legacy sign-ins in the migration dashboard.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The tenant, applications, account population, and policy settings match the requested change. Authority of record: Identity provider configuration store and application catalogue.
evidence.check_description: Compare policy targets and exclusions with tenant configuration and registered application authentication capabilities.

scenarios.action: Release a quarantined email attachment requested by the legal team
scenarios.action_context: Legal requests release of one quarantined email attachment to three named counsel before a filing deadline in forty minutes. Re-quarantine takes five minutes, but a download, malicious execution, or disclosure cannot be recalled; both the legal matter owner and security exception approver must authorize release.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The legal matter still requires the attachment and the filing deadline remains active. Authority of record: Legal matter management system.
evidence.check_description: Read matter status, filing deadline, requested attachment, and named recipients from the legal matter system.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The legal matter owner and security exception approver approved release through the specified channel. Authority of record: Security exception register.
evidence.check_description: Validate dual approval, matter identifier, attachment hash, recipients, delivery channel, and expiry.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The attachment hash, matter, recipients, and secure delivery destination are correctly bound. Authority of record: Email quarantine service and legal directory.
evidence.check_description: Match the quarantined object hash and sender metadata to the matter record and counsel directory entries.

scenarios.action: Restore an executable package blocked by endpoint protection on a build server
scenarios.action_context: A build is blocked because endpoint protection quarantined one executable package needed by a release pipeline due in ninety minutes. The package can be re-quarantined within five minutes, but executed code, produced artifacts, and audit history remain; the build owner and security exception approver control restoration.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The executable hash, repository, build server, and release pipeline match the requested restoration. Authority of record: Artifact registry and endpoint inventory.
evidence.check_description: Compare artifact provenance and hash with the registered build server and pipeline dependency graph.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The release build remains blocked solely by quarantine of the named package. Authority of record: Build orchestration platform.
evidence.check_description: Inspect build status, failed step, package reference, and quarantine dependency in the build orchestration platform.

evidence.description: Prerequisite: The build owner and security exception approver authorized restoration for this pipeline run. Authority of record: Software security exception register.
evidence.check_description: Validate both approvers, package hash, build identifier, server, permitted duration, and exception expiry.

scenarios.action: Release a supplier payment for temperature-monitoring equipment
scenarios.action_context: Accounts payable is preparing a $186,400 ACH payment to ColdTrace Instruments for 240 temperature loggers needed at three distribution centers. The bank file closes at 16:00; before submission the batch can be withdrawn in about 20 minutes, but a settled ACH may require bank recovery and supplier cooperation, with remittance reliance and audit entries remaining. The AP director may release up to $250,000, while Treasury Controls owns beneficiary verification.

evidence.description: Invoice CT-8842, supplier ColdTrace Instruments, purchase order PO-7719, and the registered beneficiary account refer to the same obligation. Authority of record: Vendor Master and Treasury Beneficiary Registry.
evidence.check_description: Join supplier tax ID, purchase order, invoice, and beneficiary fingerprint across the Vendor Master, Procurement Ledger, and Treasury Beneficiary Registry.

evidence.description: Invoice CT-8842 is posted, unmatched to any prior payment, and due in the current run. Authority of record: AP Subledger.
evidence.check_description: Reconcile invoice status, receipt quantity, and payment history across the AP Subledger and Receiving Ledger.

evidence.description: The AP director's release approval is current and within the $250,000 delegated ceiling. Authority of record: Finance Delegation Register.
evidence.check_description: Verify the approver certificate and amount ceiling against the Finance Delegation Register and the signed batch approval.

scenarios.action: Approve an urgent customer rebate before the quarter closes
scenarios.action_context: Sales finance must decide a $92,000 rebate for Northstar Retail before the 18:00 quarter-close lock. An erroneous rebate would overstate contra-revenue and change the customer's settlement expectation; the journal can be reversed the next business day, but a communicated rebate and close audit trail remain. The regional commercial finance lead has a $100,000 rebate limit, and Revenue Controls owns the program rules.

evidence.description: Northstar's qualifying purchases and accrued rebate balance support the proposed quarter-end amount. Authority of record: Rebate Accrual Ledger.
evidence.check_description: Recompute eligible sales from the Rebate Accrual Ledger and compare them with the quarter-close sales cube.

evidence.description: The regional finance lead approved the rebate within the $100,000 delegation and before close lock. Authority of record: Commercial Finance Authority Matrix.
evidence.check_description: Cross-check the digital approval, delegation tier, and close timestamp in the Commercial Finance Authority Matrix and Close Calendar.

evidence.description: The rebate belongs to Northstar, program NR-Q3, and the specified customer account and currency. Authority of record: Customer Rebate Master.
evidence.check_description: Match program code, sold-to account, currency, and rebate recipient using the Customer Rebate Master snapshot.

scenarios.action: Release a milestone payment for a partially accepted construction project
scenarios.action_context: A $1.25 million milestone payment is queued for Apex Civil after partial acceptance of a warehouse expansion. Treasury cutoff is in 90 minutes. The payment can be stopped before transmission, but after settlement recovery depends on the contractor and may delay lien releases; certification and payment records persist. The capital-project controller may release up to $1.5 million only against an accepted milestone.

evidence.description: The capital-project controller holds active authority up to $1.5 million for this project. Authority of record: Capital Expenditure Delegation Table.
evidence.check_description: Read the cached signed delegation table and verify project code, approver role, amount, and effective dates.

evidence.description: Milestone 4 has an accepted quantity, certified work value, and no prior settlement. Authority of record: Capital Projects Ledger.
evidence.check_description: Triangulate engineer certification, accepted quantities, and prior disbursements across the Capital Projects Ledger, site acceptance log, and bank-payment history.

evidence.description: Apex Civil, contract AC-2024-17, Milestone 4, and the nominated beneficiary are the intended payment scope. Authority of record: Contract Payment Register.
evidence.check_description: Query the Contract Payment Register for the contract-to-milestone-to-beneficiary binding and compare it with the queued instruction.

scenarios.action: Issue a duplicate-charge refund to a corporate cardholder
scenarios.action_context: Card operations proposes a $3,480 refund to a corporate cardholder for a duplicated conference charge. The issuer batch settles in two hours. The refund can be cancelled before batch lock in 15 minutes; after settlement it cannot be recalled without a new debit, and the cardholder may rely on the credit. A card-operations manager can approve refunds up to $5,000.

evidence.description: The card-operations manager's refund authority is active and covers $3,480. Authority of record: Card Refund Authority Service.
evidence.check_description: Query the Card Refund Authority Service for approver identity, effective dates, and transaction limit.

evidence.description: The two charge records represent one merchant transaction and no refund has already posted. Authority of record: Corporate Card Ledger.
evidence.check_description: Compare merchant reference, authorization code, amount, and posted refunds in the local Corporate Card Ledger snapshot.

evidence.description: The cardholder, duplicated transactions, original card account, and refund destination are correctly linked. Authority of record: Issuer Transaction Map.
evidence.check_description: Perform a two-source comparison between the Issuer Transaction Map and employee card assignment for account and destination consistency.

scenarios.action: Post a service credit after a documented availability breach
scenarios.action_context: Billing operations will post a $64,000 service credit to Horizon Foods after a measured availability breach. The monthly invoice is generated overnight. A wrong credit can be reversed before invoice issuance in 30 minutes, but a delivered invoice, revenue adjustment, and customer reliance remain. The service-credit committee may approve up to $75,000 under the availability schedule.

evidence.description: The committee approval is current, unanimous where required, and below the $75,000 limit. Authority of record: Service Credit Approval Archive.
evidence.check_description: Validate signatures, quorum, amount, and approval expiry across the Service Credit Approval Archive and delegation table.

evidence.description: Horizon Foods, contract HF-Cloud-9, affected service, billing account, and credit period form one approved scope. Authority of record: Contract Billing Graph.
evidence.check_description: Resolve customer, contract, service, invoice period, and billing account through the Contract Billing Graph and CRM master.

evidence.description: The measured outage minutes exceed the contract threshold and no equivalent credit is already recorded. Authority of record: SLA Measurement Ledger.
evidence.check_description: Query the SLA Measurement Ledger for outage intervals and compare the resulting credit basis with prior adjustment entries.

scenarios.action: Refund a cancelled training program to a newly supplied bank account
scenarios.action_context: Learning services owes a $12,600 program refund to twelve participants, but the organizer supplied a new bank account by email. The wire window closes in 45 minutes. A queued wire can be deleted in 10 minutes; a settled transfer to the wrong account may be irrecoverable and leaves participant reliance and investigation records. Treasury Operations must approve any destination change, regardless of amount.

evidence.description: The verified bank account belongs to the contracting organizer and is authorized to receive all participant refunds. Authority of record: Verified Beneficiary File.
evidence.check_description: Use the cached verified-beneficiary fingerprint to compare legal name, bank coordinates, contract party, and refund instruction.

evidence.description: The training program is cancelled, the refund remains unpaid, and the participant liability totals $12,600. Authority of record: Learning Revenue and Refund Ledger.
evidence.check_description: Reconcile cancellation status, participant balances, and prior refunds across the Learning Revenue Ledger and Refund Queue.

evidence.description: Treasury Operations approved the newly supplied destination after independent verification. Authority of record: Treasury Change-Control Register.
evidence.check_description: Confirm callback evidence, approver separation, delegated role, and change expiry across the Treasury Change-Control Register and verification service.

scenarios.action: Place a freight invoice on hold after a quantity mismatch
scenarios.action_context: AP proposes holding a $78,500 freight invoice after a 14-pallet quantity discrepancy. The carrier's net-10 due date is tomorrow. The hold can be removed within 15 minutes, but late-payment penalties, shipment leverage, and audit comments may remain. A freight-audit supervisor may place holds up to $100,000 while Procurement owns dispute scope.

evidence.description: Carrier, invoice, bill of lading, purchase order, and disputed pallet lines identify the same shipment. Authority of record: Logistics Payables Registry.
evidence.check_description: Query the Logistics Payables Registry for shipment-document bindings and compare identifiers with the requested hold.

evidence.description: The freight-audit supervisor is permitted to place this hold under the $100,000 threshold. Authority of record: AP Control Matrix.
evidence.check_description: Evaluate the local AP Control Matrix entry for role, hold type, amount band, and effective date.

evidence.description: The invoice quantity differs from signed delivery receipts and the invoice has not entered settlement. Authority of record: Freight Audit Workbench.
evidence.check_description: Fan out to the Freight Audit Workbench, receiving records, shipment scans, and payment queue to quantify the discrepancy and settlement state.

scenarios.action: Reject an invoice flagged as a possible duplicate of split billing
scenarios.action_context: An $118,000 facilities invoice is marked as a possible duplicate of two authorized split-billing invoices. Rejecting it could delay a valid project payment; the rejection can be reopened within one business day, but vendor notification and dispute records remain. The AP exception manager may reject invoices up to $150,000 only after split-billing review.

evidence.description: Supplier, contract, project phase, and invoice FM-908 are within the reviewed duplicate set. Authority of record: Contract Invoice Crosswalk.
evidence.check_description: Compare the Contract Invoice Crosswalk with purchase-order amendments to bind the supplier, phase, and claimed obligation.

evidence.description: The AP exception manager approved rejection within the $150,000 limit after required review. Authority of record: Invoice Exception Authority Service.
evidence.check_description: Query the Invoice Exception Authority Service for approver identity, review completion, amount limit, and expiry.

evidence.description: Invoice FM-908 is duplicative rather than an authorized third billing tranche, and no rejection is already final. Authority of record: Invoice Matching Cache.
evidence.check_description: Compare invoice fingerprints, service periods, line amounts, and split-billing references in the local Invoice Matching Cache.

scenarios.action: Hold a consulting invoice while the purchase order is being amended
scenarios.action_context: A $240,000 consulting invoice is due in three days while its purchase order is being amended from $900,000 to $1.1 million. A mistaken hold can delay a critical program and trigger interest; release takes about 30 minutes, but vendor reliance and exception history persist. The program controller can hold invoices up to $300,000 during an active amendment.

evidence.description: The consulting entity, statement of work, invoice, purchase order, and amendment request belong to one engagement. Authority of record: Engagement Control Hub.
evidence.check_description: Resolve supplier, statement-of-work, PO, amendment, and invoice identifiers across the Engagement Control Hub, sourcing platform, and vendor master.

evidence.description: The program controller has active hold authority up to $300,000 for this engagement. Authority of record: Program Finance Delegation Register.
evidence.check_description: Compare the controller's signed approval and engagement delegation with the central Finance Delegation Register.

evidence.description: The purchase-order amendment remains open and the invoice is not already blocked or paid. Authority of record: Consulting Payables Ledger.
evidence.check_description: Query the Consulting Payables Ledger for PO amendment state, invoice workflow, existing holds, and settlement status.

scenarios.action: Replace a supplier beneficiary account following an emailed change request
scenarios.action_context: Vendor maintenance proposes replacing the beneficiary for a supplier expecting a $410,000 payment tomorrow; the request arrived from an email address used previously by the supplier. An incorrect change can divert funds. The master-data update can be rolled back in 20 minutes before payment extraction, but any released transfer and fraud investigation trail remain. Treasury Master Data and a separate supplier relationship owner must approve changes above $100,000.

evidence.description: Treasury Master Data and the supplier relationship owner both approved the change under the high-value dual-control rule. Authority of record: Beneficiary Change Authority Vault.
evidence.check_description: Verify independent approvals, callback attestation, role separation, and expiry through the Beneficiary Change Authority Vault and supplier-contact registry.

evidence.description: The new account is owned by the contracted supplier and applies to the named legal entity, currency, and payment route. Authority of record: Vendor Beneficiary Master.
evidence.check_description: Compare bank-account fingerprint, legal name, tax identity, currency, and company code against the local verified Vendor Beneficiary Master.

evidence.description: No payment file has been extracted and the proposed account-change request is the active supplier instruction. Authority of record: Payment Readiness and Change Queue.
evidence.check_description: Cross-check payment-extract status and the active change request across the Payment Readiness service and Vendor Change Queue.

scenarios.action: Update payroll settlement instructions for a newly acquired subsidiary
scenarios.action_context: Payroll treasury must update settlement instructions for a newly acquired subsidiary's 2,800 employees before the payroll file locks at 13:00. A wrong route could misdirect approximately $8.4 million in net pay. Instructions can be restored within 20 minutes before lock; after transmission, recall is uncertain and employee reliance, bank files, and audit records remain. The group treasurer and payroll controller jointly authorize subsidiary settlement changes.

evidence.description: Joint group-treasurer and payroll-controller authority covers the subsidiary and current pay cycle. Authority of record: Payroll Settlement Mandate.
evidence.check_description: Validate the cached signed Payroll Settlement Mandate for both roles, entity, cycle, limits, and effective dates.

evidence.description: The subsidiary payroll is approved, remains before file lock, and has no competing settlement instruction. Authority of record: Group Payroll Control Plane.
evidence.check_description: Fan out to payroll approval, file-lock status, bank calendar, and instruction-version history in the Group Payroll Control Plane.

evidence.description: Subsidiary legal entity, payroll file, funding account, clearing bank, and employee population are correctly bound. Authority of record: Payroll Banking Directory.
evidence.check_description: Query the Payroll Banking Directory for entity-to-account and file-routing bindings, then compare the instruction checksum.

scenarios.action: Change the refund destination for a closed customer account
scenarios.action_context: Customer finance proposes sending a $22,000 refund from a closed commercial account to a replacement destination nominated during closure. The refund batch starts in 70 minutes. The instruction can be removed before lock in 10 minutes; a settled transfer may not be recoverable, and closure correspondence and accounting entries persist. A customer-finance manager may approve up to $25,000, but destination changes require closure-team confirmation.

evidence.description: The nominated destination belongs to the former account owner and is tied to the closure case and refund obligation. Authority of record: Closure Destination Crosswalk.
